text: Register the plugin marketplace using `claude plugin marketplace add tester-army/e2e`.
Install the plugin using `claude plugin install e2e@e2e`.
Start a new Claude Code session after installation.
Inspect the newly written screenshot.
Commit the screenshot alongside the tests.
Run the test again so the stored screenshot serves as the comparison baseline.
DeepSeek V4 refuses forced tool choice during agent steps.
Meta Muse Spark refuses forced tool choice during agent steps.
Read the authentication token from `request.env` provided to `DeviceProvider.acquire`.
Do not retrieve the authentication token directly from `process.env`.
For local development, use an existing subscription login (e.g. `npx e2e login openai`) or configure an AI SDK provider with the required credentials and environment variables.
In CI, provide the model provider's API key through CI secrets.
A CI job exposes its API key to executed tests, configuration, and dependencies, so keys must be restricted to trusted builds.
Run untrusted pull-request code without secrets or write tokens.
Configure `app.launchArguments` with `--initialUrl` pointing to the Expo development server.
Set `camera: 'grant'` in `app.permissions` to grant camera access without a system permission prompt.
Begin each test with `app.open()`, because the initial warm-up does not apply the configured launch arguments or permissions.
Start exploration with `npx e2e explore --session <name>` using a named session saved by a setup test.
The explorer runs only the corresponding setup test and restores its saved session before exploration begins.
Authenticate in setup using a session cookie via `browser.setCookies` instead of filling a secret, because a secret fill disables screenshots for the restored exploration.
The decision-model executor selects the `type` operation and identifies the target field from the latest screen observation.
A separate text model generates the input value using the goal, parameters, field label, and page text.
The executor enters exactly the generated string into the selected field.
The built-in `maestro` job type runs Maestro flows, not e2e tests.
Running e2e tests in EAS Workflows requires custom jobs.
After two minutes in the EAS Simulators queue, e2e logs `still queued at EAS after two minutes`.
The telemetry request has a two-second deadline when an e2e command finishes.
The Ubuntu image includes the Android AVD `emulator` (API 34).
The Ubuntu image includes the Android AVD `emulator-35`.
The Ubuntu image includes the Android AVD `emulator-36`.
Limrun provides five device configuration options: `region`, `hardTimeout`, `ios.model`, `android.model`, and `android.osVersion`.
`region`: Limrun selects the region by default; a preferred region such as `eu` may overflow to another region when capacity is limited.
`hardTimeout`: Limits maximum device lifetime, including abandoned runs; defaults to `1h` and accepts Go-style durations.

`ios.model` and `android.model`: Limrun selects models by default, with `iphone` or `ipad` for iOS and `phone` or `tablet` for Android. `android.osVersion` defaults to `15` and serves as a scheduling hint.
A `mutates: true` project tool call consumes one action slot before execution, even if the call fails.
A pre-page script prepares browser behavior before the application starts.
Examples include mocking a browser API, seeding `Math.random`, or setting a flag that the application reads at boot.
The failure recap shows the recording's file path, or its URL if a hosted browser retains the video remotely.
Use Node.js `fs` for filesystem operations.
Use an appropriate database client for database operations.
`locator.and(other)` and `locator.or(other)` are unsupported and have no direct equivalents.
Playwright's `locator.locator('css')` method is unsupported in e2e.
Use scoped semantic queries for nested selectors, such as `cell.getByRole('textbox')`.
Chain `getByRole(...)` after `browser.locator('css')`, or express the entire selector path in a single `browser.locator` selector.
Restricting `browser.evaluate` to JSON input and output values allows e2e to record and redact the result in the test report.
Replace Maestro's `tapOn: "Save"` with `screen.getByText('Save').tap()`.
Replace conditional `runFlow` with `if (await locator.isVisible()) { ... }`.
Maestro uses case-insensitive regex matching and taps the first match; e2e uses exact, case-sensitive string matching and raises `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` for multiple matches.
Use `{ exact: false }` or a regular expression for flexible text matching, and `.first()` or `{ visible: true }` to narrow multiple matches.
Use `pressSequentially()` instead of `fill()` for autocomplete fields that depend on keyboard events.
`fill()` sets the field value without emitting keyboard events.
`pressSequentially()` uses the platform keyboard and supports a delay between characters.
If no text-accepting field has focus, a custom engine's `EngineKeyboard.type` must throw `NOT_ACTIONABLE` instead of silently discarding input.
`locator.nth()` throws `INVALID_LOCATOR` when the index is negative or not an integer.
Custom resource setup runs before any `beforeEach` hook executes.
Custom resource setup counts against the test timeout.
A failure during custom resource setup is reported in the `beforeEach` phase, even if no `beforeEach` hook has started.
Each engine maps its platform-specific element types to e2e's shared, closed Role vocabulary.
The shared Role vocabulary gives the same role query consistent meaning across browser and device targets.
An `agent.act` instruction must contain 1–8192 UTF-8 bytes after NFC normalization.
`expect(locator).toBeVisible()` repeatedly checks for a visible element until the condition is met or the timeout expires.
If no element appears, `toBeVisible()` eventually fails with `ASSERTION_FAILED`; a hidden element also keeps it waiting.
`locator.isVisible()` checks the current state immediately and returns `false` if the element is absent or hidden.
Without `--update-snapshots`, an assertion against a baseline written earlier in the same run fails with `ASSERTION_FAILED` until the next run.
A negated screenshot assertion cannot pass against a baseline written earlier in the same run, even with `--update-snapshots`.
With `--update-snapshots`, a positive assertion can compare against a same-run baseline and may rewrite it.
A client disconnect or termination signal returns exit status `0`.
An uncaught error returns exit status `1`.
Invalid command-line arguments return exit status `2`.
Startup failures return the underlying error's category-specific exit status.
Press `f` to rerun previously unsuccessful tests, including those outside the current positional and `p` selection.
Press `u` to rerun the current selection with `--update-snapshots`.
Press `p` to select a file, bare name, or glob for subsequent runs.
Press `t` to filter tests by a test-title pattern.
The security policy forbids serializing secret values into JSON.
When a `Secret` handle reaches a JSON sink, e2e rejects the operation with `POLICY_DENIED`.
`GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` and `GITHUB_REF` identify the pull request; the event payload also supplies its head commit.
`GITHUB_WORKFLOW` and `GITHUB_JOB` form the marker used to find and update the reporter's existing comment on reruns.
`GITHUB_REPOSITORY` and `GITHUB_RUN_ID` are used to construct artifact links.
Under `on-all-retries`, e2e retains a trace page for each test that was retried.
Under `on-all-retries`, video captures every attempt after the first, but not the initial attempt.
If a test is never retried, neither a trace page nor a video is produced under `on-all-retries`.
Configure `maxObservationBytes` on each relevant named agent under `agents`.
Configure `maxInputTokens` on each relevant named agent under `agents`.
Each worker constructs its own agents from the configuration module.
The report stores the largest per-agent observation budget in `run.limits.maxObservationBytes` and the largest input-token budget in `run.limits.maxModelTokensPerCall`.
A live AI SDK `ModelInstance` provides the `doGenerate` method for generation calls, rather than only the identifying fields `specificationVersion`, `provider`, and `modelId`.
Manually add the custom results directory to `.gitignore`, because `e2e init` only creates ignore entries for the default `.e2e/` paths.
Each worker constructs its own custom `store` instance, so workers cannot rely on sharing a single constructed instance.
The target's `app` fields explicitly accept `undefined` in their types, allowing direct use of `process.env` values even when the variables are unset.
`WORKER_EXIT` indicates that a worker terminated unexpectedly during test-file execution.
The test in flight fails with `WORKER_CRASH`.
The remaining tests in the affected file are skipped.
Attempts completed before the worker exit remain in the report, including earlier retries and completed serial-group members.
Call `browser.keyboard.down(key)` again while the same key is still held to emit a key-repeat event.
`smol()` uses `mcr.microsoft.com` as the outbound destination for its Playwright image.
`e2e init` contacts the package registry when installing dependencies.
Register `browser.onDialog` before triggering the native JavaScript dialog.
A custom dialog handler must call either `dialog.accept()` or `dialog.dismiss()`.
If the custom handler does neither, e2e dismisses the dialog and reports `APP_NOT_OPEN` on the next step, not during handler registration.
On iOS, changing a permission terminates a running app, so `device.setPermission()` should be called before `app.open()`.
On Android, revoking a permission terminates a running app, so permissions should be changed before `app.open()`.
Configured `app.permissions` are reapplied on every fresh launch of the pinned app, including `app.open()` and `app.restart()`.
`app.clearState()` resets app data and permissions, and the configured `app.permissions` are applied on the fresh launch.
A timed-out `agent-device` command continues running on the device because these commands do not support abort signals.
The next test attempt must wait for the timed-out command to settle before proceeding.
Only the two permitted failure codes may be retryable because they describe repeatable reads.
If another failure code claims retryability, the runner coerces it into a non-retryable `ENGINE_FAILURE`.
Both `actions` and `location` depend on `observation` because their node references use identifiers from the observation's ID space.
Provisioning may require a first-run download whose duration depends on the network.
A premature timeout in `prepare()` could prevent all subsequent tests from running.
For web targets, `validateApp()` receives the URL, while `prepare()` and `init()` receive only the site through `info.app.site`.
For web targets, the URL is opened later through `session.open()`, not during `prepare()` or `init()`.
For device targets, `prepare()` and `init()` receive the declared `bundleId`, `appPath`, `launchArguments`, and `permissions`.
Device warm-up passes no launch arguments and does not modify permissions.
Developers can choose either the Next.js App Router or the Astro example; both use runner-started web apps tested in Chromium.
Follow the selected project's README to install, build, and run the example.
Locator tests require no AI model and can run without `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`.
Agent tests are skipped unless `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` is set.
